---
title: "Mobile Store Screenshots"
description: "How the App Store, Google Play and Microsoft Store screenshots, graphics and the roadmap feature previews are captured from the real Flutter UI and composed into images."
updatedAt: "2026-11-24"
audience: developers
---

Store images come from two stages. The first stage captures the real app UI from
Flutter widget tests with synthetic fixture data. The second stage composes those
captures into branded store images. Re-run both stages after any visible change to
the app shell or to a listed screen.

## 1. Raw capture (Flutter)

`apps/mobile/test/store_screenshots/store_screenshots_test.dart` pumps eight real
feature pages (dashboard, tasks, calendar, assistant, finance, habits, time
tracker, notes) inside `StoreScreenshotApp`, which is the app's own root frame
in the default Sorbet theme (`SorbetTheme()`), light for the store listings.
It renders each page in English and Vietnamese at every store device size in
`storeDevices`.

- Each page reads fixture data from `screens/<id>_screen.dart` and
  `fixtures/`: one fictional design team ("Sorbet Studio") with dates relative to
  the capture day. Fixtures never use real accounts, real data or a backend.
- Apple guideline 2.3.3 requires the screenshots to show the real UI. Never
  replace a page with drawn UI. If a page cannot render from fixtures, capture
  it on a device against the seeded local backend
  (`integration_test/e2e_flows_test.dart`, `E2E_SHOT` markers).
- Every capture passes `expectCleanStoreCapture` (`capture_guard.dart`) after
  its PNG is written. It fails when the screen shows a load error ("Something
  went wrong" or Home's "Pull down to try again") or any fixture string from
  the other locale. `StoreLocale.pick` records each EN/VI pair, so a new
  fixture string is covered automatically. Fix a failure in the fixture. Never
  crop around it.
- The design render harness loads Nunito, Noto Sans and JetBrains Mono. Sorbet's
  overline and numeric roles use JetBrains Mono, and without it those runs draw
  as solid blocks.
- Root tabs (Home, Assistant) are built by `ShellPage` itself and ignore the
  shell's `child`. Pass their fixture page through `storeShellFrame`'s
  `homePageBuilder` or `assistantPageBuilder`.
- The app cache (`CacheStore.instance`) is one singleton for the whole run,
  and its cache keys do not carry the listing locale
  (`currentCacheLocaleTag()` reads the host locale). Fixture ids that reach a
  cache key carry the locale (`StoreTasksFixture.boardId(locale)`,
  `StoreTeam.localeWorkspaceId(locale)`), so EN data never shows in VI. Seed
  cache snapshots only from `initStoreCache` in `setUpAll`. A cache write
  started inside a widget test's fake-async zone never completes once that
  test ends, and every later write queues behind it and hangs the run.

Run it on a host with Flutter (not on a machine that is short on disk):

```bash
cd apps/mobile
DESIGN_RENDER_DIR=$PWD/build/store_raw \
  flutter test test/store_screenshots/store_screenshots_test.dart
```

PNGs land in `build/store_raw/<store>/<device>/<locale>/NN-<id>.png` at the
store pixel size (logical size × pixel ratio). Filter a run with
comma-separated `STORE_SCREENS`, `STORE_DEVICES` (`ios/iphone-6.9`) or
`STORE_LOCALES`. `STORE_SHOWCASE=1` adds the roadmap preview targets. Without `DESIGN_RENDER_DIR`, the suite runs as a smoke test on
one phone size and one desktop size and writes nothing.

## 2. Composition (Playwright)

```bash
node scripts/store-screenshots/compose.mjs --raw apps/mobile/build/store_raw
node scripts/store-screenshots/validate.mjs
```

`compose.mjs` renders each capture in headless Chromium as a colour-field
card, with no device frame and no status bar:

- a pastel Sorbet field with a warm white wave rising from the bottom. The
  wave crest shifts slightly by frame index, so a locale's set reads as one
  strip, and the field carries no other hue;
- a caption: a product-label chip (JetBrains Mono, uppercase) over a Nunito
  900 headline of at most two lines;
- the raw capture as a frameless rounded card with a soft shadow, bleeding off
  the canvas edge. The dashboard frame fans three cards (calendar, assistant
  and the dashboard on top) on the `stack` layout and two (the calendar behind
  a 74% wide dashboard card) on the `tablet` layout, and the
  assistant frame carries a "Calendar updated" chip pointing at its calendar
  action card. The Flutter capture writes that card's position beside the PNG
  (`NN-assistant.json`), and the chip repeats a state the capture shows.

Each target in `specs.mjs` names a `layout` for its canvas shape; the numbers
live in `template-layout.mjs` as percentages of the canvas width.

| Layout | Targets | Composition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `stack` | iPhone 6.9/6.3/6.5, iPhone Duo outer, Play phone, Play 7" tablet | Caption centred above the card |
| `tablet` | iPad 13", Play 10" tablet | Caption above a wide card (84% of the width); a cropped card is 88% wide |
| `side` | iPhone Duo inner (2853x2007) | Caption left, card right, a thin centre line on the card |
| `window` | Mac, Windows | Caption left, a plain window card (neutral grey dots) right |

A tablet page can end before its screen does: Home lists at most three tasks
and three events, and Finance lists six transactions beside two month tiles.
Those two captures write a `content` anchor beside the PNG
(`NN-<id>.json`, `storeContentAnchor` in `store_screenshot_app.dart`) that
marks where the page's last block ends. The composer then crops the card to
that height and widens it to 88%, so the card ends just after the content with
the field and wave visible below it. Pages the real tablet layout can fill
(habits, notes) instead list more fixture rows on the two tablet targets
(`storeTabletListing`), and phones, desktops and the 7" tablet keep their
fixtures.

Headlines, overlines and the assistant chip come from
`scripts/store-screenshots/store-captions.json`, keyed by screen id. The
`screenshots` captions in `apps/mobile/store/metadata/<store>.json` carry the
same headline text, and `validate.test.mjs` fails when they differ. Screens run
in story order for every target (dashboard, assistant, tasks, calendar, time
tracker, finance, habits, notes); the iPhone Duo sets keep the first four.
Outputs:

- `apps/mobile/store/screenshots/<store>/<device>/<locale>/NN-<id>.jpg`: JPEG,
  quality 84, RGB with no alpha, at the exact size in `specs.mjs`. Microsoft
  Store targets (`format: 'png'`) write `NN-<id>.png` as 24-bit PNG with no
  alpha at 1920x1080. The metadata `files` paths and
  `scripts/store-metadata` expect `.png` for `windows`.
- `apps/mobile/store/screenshots/layout-report.json`: the measured caption box,
  card box, chip box and size, headline size and line count of every
  screenshot, its canvas size and the sha256 of the image.
  compose measures each caption in the browser and merges the entries it
  writes into the file.
- `apps/mobile/store/screenshots/<platform>/web/NN-<id>.webp` and a
  `manifest.json` with each file's width and height: up to six EN shots per
  platform for /roadmap, at most 1280 px on the long edge and 150 KB each. The
  listing's `gallery` entries choose the screens.
- `apps/mobile/store/graphics/android/feature-graphic-1024x500.png` and
  `apps/mobile/store/graphics/windows/hero-1920x1080.png`: 24-bit PNG with no
  alpha. The hero carries no text, and the feature graphic shows only the app
  name.

Options: `--only ios/iphone-6.9,macos/mac`, `--locales en`, `--no-graphics` and
`--gallery-only` (rebuilds only the web gallery from the composed screenshots,
leaving them byte-for-byte unchanged).
Captions use Nunito and JetBrains Mono from Google Fonts, so composition needs
network access. Playwright and sharp resolve from a workspace that depends on
them. Run `bunx playwright install chromium` once per host.

Section 5 lists what `validate.mjs` checks.

## 3. Roadmap feature previews

The /roadmap page shows the real app in light and dark Sorbet on generic device
frames. The previews come from the same capture suite as the store images.

```bash
cd apps/mobile
DESIGN_RENDER_DIR=$PWD/build/store_raw STORE_SHOWCASE=1 \
  flutter test --concurrency=2 test/store_screenshots/store_screenshots_test.dart
cd ../..
node scripts/store-screenshots/showcase.mjs --raw apps/mobile/build/store_raw
```

`showcaseDevices` (Flutter) and `SHOWCASE_DEVICES` (`specs.mjs`) hold the
device table, and a test keeps their sizes in step. `showcaseScreens` lists the
screens (`SHOWCASE.screens`): tasks board, task detail, calendar, Mira
assistant, dashboard and time tracker. The task detail page loads its
description in a WebView that widget tests cannot render, so the capture shows
the fixture's empty description state, not drawn UI.

| Device | Logical size | Ratio | Frame | Export long edge |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `iphone` | 393x852 | 3x | phone | 1280 px |
| `ipad` | 1024x1366 | 2x | tablet | 1600 px |
| `ipad-landscape` | 1366x1024 | 2x | tablet | 1600 px |
| `mac` | 1512x982 | 2x | macOS window | 1600 px |
| `duo-folded` | 466x678 | 3x | phone | 1280 px |
| `duo-unfolded` | 951x669 | 3x | foldable with centre crease | 1600 px |

`duo-folded` and `duo-unfolded` are the iPhone Duo outer and inner displays.
Each preview is a frameless rounded card with a soft shadow on a transparent
canvas: no device art, no status bar, no field and no headline, so the page
supplies captions and the background. The Mac preview is a plain window card
with a white title strip and three neutral grey dots, and the open iPhone Duo
keeps a thin centre line.

`showcase.mjs` renders each capture on a transparent canvas in headless
Chromium and encodes AVIF (primary) and WebP (fallback) with sharp, at the
highest quality in `SHOWCASE.avifQualities` / `webpQualities` that fits
90 KB (AVIF) and 140 KB (WebP). Output:

```text
packages/roadmap-core/src/assets/previews/app/<screen>/<device>-<theme>-<locale>.avif
packages/roadmap-core/src/assets/previews/app/<screen>/<device>-<theme>-<locale>.webp
packages/roadmap-core/src/assets/previews/app/manifest.json
```

`manifest.json` is `{ generatedAt, items: [{ screen, device, theme, locale,
width, height, avif, webp, avifBytes, webpBytes }] }` with repository-relative
paths. Options: `--devices`, `--themes`, `--locales`, `--screens` and `--out`;
a filtered run keeps the entries of files already written.
`showcase-checks.mjs` (run by `validate.mjs` and `showcase.test.mjs`) requires
the full set, sizes that match the manifest, an alpha channel in both formats,
the long-edge and byte budgets and no stray files.

## 4. Store requirements

The store sizes live in `SCREENSHOT_TARGETS` (`specs.mjs`) and the limits in
`store-rules.mjs`. Sources:

- Apple: [screenshot specifications](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/app-information/screenshot-specifications)
- iPhone Duo: [specifications](https://www.apple.com/iphone-duo/specs/)
- Google Play: [add preview assets](https://support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/9866151)

| Target | Size | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ios/iphone-6.9` | 1320x2868 | Large Dynamic Island display (1260x2736, 1290x2796 or 1320x2868) |
| `ios/iphone-6.3` | 1206x2622 | Required: "At least one screenshot for iPhone with Dynamic Island (medium display)" at 1179x2556 or 1206x2622 |
| `ios/iphone-6.5` | 1284x2778 | Needed only when large-display shots are missing; kept because it is cheap |
| `ios/iphone-duo-outer` | 1398x2034 | iPhone Duo outer display, portrait (2034x1398 also accepted) |
| `ios/iphone-duo-inner` | 2853x2007 | iPhone Duo inner display, landscape (2007x2853 also accepted) |
| `ios/ipad-13` | 2064x2752 | Required when the app supports iPadOS |
| `macos/mac` | 2880x1800 | Also 1280x800, 1440x900 or 2560x1600 |
| `windows/desktop` | 1920x1080 | Opaque PNG |
| `android/phone` | 1080x1920 | 2-8 per locale |
| `android/tablet7` | 1080x1920 | At least 4, each side at least 1080, 9:16 or 16:9 |
| `android/tablet10` | 1440x2560 | At least 4, each side at least 1080, 9:16 or 16:9 |

The iPhone Duo page lists the inner display at "1878-by-2670-pixel resolution
at 430 ppi" and the outer display at "1398-by-2034" at 460 ppi. App Store
Connect lists "1398 × 2034 pixels, 2034 × 1398 pixels (outer display);
2007 × 2853 pixels, 2853 × 2007 pixels (inner display)" and notes: "Starting in
April 2027, screenshots will be required for any app using the iOS 27.1 SDK or
later." Submitting Duo screenshots shows a "made for iPhone Duo" badge. The Duo
targets carry four screens per locale: the dashboard, assistant, tasks and
calendar.

Apple accepts JPEG or PNG with no alpha, 1-10 per device size. Google Play
takes JPEG or 24-bit PNG with no alpha, at most 8 MB each, each side 320-3840
px and an aspect ratio of at most 2.3:1. Google Play does not require a
foldable set, so none ships. `apps/mobile/store` is the source of truth for
store images; there is no fastlane metadata tree, and the mobile deploy
workflow does not upload screenshots.

## 5. Validation

`validate.mjs` (also run by `scripts/store-screenshots/validate.test.mjs` and
`store-rules.test.mjs` in `bun test:scripts`) checks:

- exact sizes, each target's format and RGB channels (no greyscale or CMYK);
- colour profile: sRGB or untagged only. Display P3, Adobe RGB and any other
  ICC profile fail;
- Google Play side lengths, aspect ratio, the 9:16 or 16:9 ratio for tablets and
  the 8 MB cap;
- per-locale counts for each device class, and the same set in English and
  Vietnamese;
- caption layout from `layout-report.json`: every screenshot has an entry sized
  like its image whose `sha256` matches the file (a stale report fails), and
  each caption keeps at least 5% of the width and height clear on every edge,
  runs at most two lines, has a headline of at least 4.2% of the canvas width
  on phones and 2.6% on iPad, Mac and Windows, and stays clear of the
  measured card box. The assistant's chip stays inside that card box, with
  text of at least 2.6% of the width on phones and 1.6% elsewhere;
- per-store file limits, opaque graphics, the web gallery limits and the 40 MiB
  budget for committed screenshots;
- that every screenshot the metadata lists exists for each store that has any
  screenshot committed. Stores can land one at a time;
- the roadmap previews (section 3).

Run `node scripts/store-metadata/validate.mjs --require-assets` as well: it
checks that the metadata lists every committed screenshot.
